land.text: the Tafilalt, where Sufri Kharijites settled Sijilmasa 'after the Berber revolts against the Umayyads'

predecessors.note: The infobox names the Umayyad Caliphate as the predecessor; the Umayyads had fallen in 750, and the Berber revolts (739-743) had already cut the Maghreb off, so the land is entered as nobody's.

land.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt: the dynasty 'fragmented' into 'a hostile takeover by the Maghrawa Berbers, former clients of the Cordoban caliphate'

capitals.name: Sijilmasa
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Sijilmasa'; built 757 (Sijilmasa page). Coordinates are those of the Tafilalt oasis (Rissani), approximate: the gazetteer has Sijilmasa as a place.

rulers.name: Isa ibn Mazyad al-Aswad
rulers.note: '757/8-772'; al-Bakri: elected leader and later executed after ruling 14 years.

rulers.name: Yasah ibn Midrar
rulers.note: killed 'in that year or the next' during the Fatimid siege (Sijilmasa page).

correction.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt oasis region, 'built 757'; the only territory the Midrarid page names is the Tafilalt

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area (infobox area empty) and names no other territory (the Draa, Sous and Ziz are not mentioned), so the shape is the Tafilalt region (56,000 km2), the gazetteer's 'Sijilmasa (region)'. The infobox also lists the dynasty as a nominal vassal of the Abbasids to 906 and of the Fatimids 906-976, which is not a loss of land.

region.text: Sijilmasa and the Tafilalt, settled by Sufri Kharijites after the Berber revolts

ledger.note: 757: Sufri Kharijites found Sijilmasa and the Midrarid line begins. Infobox 'Sijilmasa built: 757'; Samgu 'led the establishment of the town of Sijilmasa in 757/8'; the ruler list opens with Isa ibn Mazyad al-Aswad, 757/8-772.

909: the Fatimid army besieges Sijilmasa. 'Abu 'Abdallah's army arrived in the Tafilalt in the latter half of 909, and laid siege to the city'; the Midrarid Yasa' was killed 'in that year or the next'.
909: the Fatimids install a vassal. The ruler list gives Wasul ibn Thakiyya from 909 after Yasah, and the infobox makes the dynasty a 'Vassal of the Fatimid Caliphate (906-976)'.

976: the Midrarid emirate ends. Infobox 'Fatimid annexation: 976'; the lede: fragmentation 'eventually resulted in a hostile takeover by the Maghrawa Berbers, former clients of the Cordoban caliphate'. The Sijilmasa page dates neither.

wars.name: Fatimid conquest of Sijilmasa
wars.outcome: The Fatimid army besieged Sijilmasa in the second half of 909; the Midrarid Yasa' was killed 'in that year or the next', and the dynasty continued as a Fatimid vassal under Wasul ibn Thakiyya (909-913).
wars.note: Al-Mahdi and al-Qa'im had hidden in the city for four years from 905 'under the countenance of the Midrar rulers' (Sijilmasa page).

wars.name: Maghrawa takeover of Sijilmasa
wars.outcome: The Midrarid dynasty ended in 976 (infobox: Fatimid annexation) by a hostile takeover of the Maghrawa Berbers.
wars.note: Neither page names the Maghrawa leader or the month; the Zirid dossier has Buluggin dying at Sijilmasa in 984 after taking the western Maghreb by 980.

certainty.note: An oasis emirate on the edge of the Sahara: no page gives a frontier.

notes: Cliopatria has no Midrarid row. The Midrarid page names only the Tafilalt as territory; any wider Midrarid hold on the Draa or the Sous is not on the pages opened. Start 757 is the founding of Sijilmasa; the page says the city 'asserted its independence' from the Abbasids 'as early as 771' (Sijilmasa page) and lists the dynasty's status as nominal Abbasid vassal 757-906 and Fatimid vassal 906-976: those vassal relations are the Abbasid and Fatimid dossiers' to record (me-08), and no event is entered here. End 976 is the infobox's 'Fatimid annexation', which sits uneasily with the Maghrawa takeover in the lede; no page gives a month or a named conqueror. The Maghrawa (Zenata of Fez and Sijilmasa, 909-1269 per the infobox) need a dossier: slug 'maghrawa'. The ruler list of 19 is the page's, with the slashed years reduced to the first year. Gazetteer: Tafilalt resolves; Sijilmasa is a place there.
